"The initial landings took place at 0830 while our task group remained from 28 to 50 miles East of the island ... providing air support and guarding against any possible fleet action by the enemy." (Okinawa)
"At 1603 we took picket station #2 with center of formation bearing 100°T, 12 miles."
"an enemy plane was discovered approaching the T.G. This was shot down by C.A.P. before it could come in."
"several enemy planes were picked up by radar. Four of these were shot down by C.A.P. and the rest turned away."
"At 1700 we took picket station #1, 12 miles bearing 060°T from our group."
"1232 C/C to 020°T ... The SC-3 radar picked up bogey at 010°, distance 22 miles ... Fighters vectored out from task group merged with bogey on scope until raid had passed close aboard port beam."

"1245 the sound of dog-fight and MG fire was heard ... suddenly a Judy appeared in a very steep dive, out of the clouds, with two friendly Corsairs ... speed was increased to 25 knots ... The bomb fell harmlessly into the water about 1000yds abeam."

"Judy ... finally hit in main radio transmitter room, causing large fires" (frames 65-88, main deck house; radio transmitter room, main radio and CIC ruptured and scorched; all radio and radar equipment destroyed or inoperative; galley scorched; flag bags and signal flags destroyed). The diary gives no time for the hit: placed at 1255, after the 1245 dog-fight and before the fires were under control (about 1300)
